sourcedFrom: NOMAD Ti XC  SERIES  OWNERS MANUAL — Rev071824 (UNKNOWN — not printed in the document)
cleanIntro: Dead Air's published service for this titanium Nomad is the mount hardware and nothing deeper: the rear adapter, the front cap, the threads and tapers they seat on, and the inspection that catches a loose or misaligned part before it becomes a baffle strike. The book publishes no procedure that opens the baffle core, and nothing here asks you to.

steps.title: Unloaded, magazine out — and never on a closed action
steps.action: Before the suppressor is handled, check the chamber and make certain the firearm is unloaded with the magazine removed. If there is any doubt about how, the clearing procedure is in your rifle's own operator's manual, and Dead Air rules out fitting a suppressor to a firearm with a closed action.
steps.prose: This can goes on many different rifles and their clearing drills differ; only the host's book has yours. An open action is how you see the chamber is empty while your hands are at the muzzle.
steps.quote: CHECK YOUR WEAPON’S CHAMBER AND MAKE CERTAIN THAT THE WEAPON IS UNLOADED AND THE MAGAZINE REMOVED BEFORE PROCEEDING ANY FURTHER.
steps.cite: NOMAD Ti XC  SERIES  OWNERS MANUAL — Rev071824 — 1. PRODUCT OVERVIEW, printed p.5
steps.warn: DO NOT INSTALL YOUR NEW SUPPRESSOR ON A FIREARM WITH A CLOSED ACTION!

steps.title: Let it cool before you touch it
steps.action: Wait until the suppressor is cold before you grip it. If it has to come off while still too hot to touch, the hook spanner wrench is the tool for it, not your hand.
steps.prose: A titanium can holds heat long after the last shot and it burns through gloves. Hot threads also bind, which is the moment people reach for force they should not use.
steps.quote: THE SUPPRESSOR MAY BECOME EXTREMELY HOT AFTER USE. NEVER GRAB A HOT SUPPRESSOR AS IT CAN RESULT IN BURNS AND INJURY.
steps.cite: NOMAD Ti XC  SERIES  OWNERS MANUAL — Rev071824 — 7. INSTALLATION AND REMOVAL, printed p.11

steps.title: Ceiling — nothing hotter than .300 Norma Magnum from 22 inches
steps.action: Confirm what has been and will be fired through it. Unless the suppressor itself or its packaging says otherwise, its ceiling is the pressure of .300 Norma Magnum with a 22-inch barrel; anything above that is outside what the can is built for.
steps.prose: ⛔ This ceiling is printed in the book you are working from. If your can or its box states a different rating, the marking on the can is the one Dead Air tells you to follow.
steps.quote: UNLESS STATED OTHERWISE ON THE SUPPRESSOR ITSELF OR ON THE PACKAGING, THE SUPPRESSOR WILL NOT FUNCTION SAFELY WITH ANY CARTRIDGE WITH PRESSURES HIGHER THAN .300 NORMA MAGNUM WITH A BARREL LENGTH OF 22 INCHES.
steps.cite: NOMAD Ti XC  SERIES  OWNERS MANUAL — Rev071824 — 7. INSTALLATION AND REMOVAL, printed p.9

steps.title: Which way is which
steps.action: Throughout this procedure "back" is toward the rifle and "front" is away from it. The thread mount goes in the back of the suppressor and the front cap threads into the front.
steps.prose: Dead Air defines the words because the adapter steps turn two parts in opposite directions at once, and an unclear "turn it left" is how threads get forced the wrong way.
steps.quote: When discussing directionality during assembly, “back” will always be toward the host weapon, “front” will always be away.
steps.cite: NOMAD Ti XC  SERIES  OWNERS MANUAL — Rev071824 — 3. ADAPTER INSTALLATION, printed p.6

steps.title: Off the rifle — counter-clockwise, unless the thread is left-hand
steps.action: With a direct-thread adapter fitted, rotate the body of the suppressor counter-clockwise until it starts to unthread from the muzzle. A left-hand thread unscrews clockwise. With a KeyMo adapter, turn the body counter-clockwise about three-quarters of a turn until it stops, then slip it off the brake or flash hider.
steps.prose: Know your barrel's thread before you put force on it. Turning a left-hand thread the usual way only tightens it, and a can that will not move is telling you that.
steps.quote: To remove the suppressor when the Direct Thread Adapter is installed, simply rotate the body of the suppressor counter-clockwise until it begins to unthread from the muzzle of the host weapon.
steps.cite: NOMAD Ti XC  SERIES  OWNERS MANUAL — Rev071824 — 7. INSTALLATION AND REMOVAL, printed p.11

steps.title: Field strip complete — off the host
steps.action: With the suppressor off the rifle, the routine service is done at this point: wipe the outside and check the mount before it goes back on. Taking the adapter or the front cap off is the deeper service, and Dead Air publishes nothing past those two parts.
steps.prose: The deep lane covers the adapter and the front cap, exactly as far as the book goes and no further.
steps.quote: Any questions concerning the performance or care of your suppressor should be directed to our Customer Service Department at 801-857-4232.
steps.cite: NOMAD Ti XC  SERIES  OWNERS MANUAL — Rev071824 — 7. INSTALLATION AND REMOVAL, printed p.11

deepSteps.title: Adapter off: spanners in OPPOSITE directions
deepSteps.action: Catch the notches with the hook spanners so the adapter turns counter-clockwise while the suppressor turns clockwise. Set the hooks an inch or two apart and squeeze them together for leverage, then keep loosening until the mount comes out of the back of the can.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ Two spanners in opposite directions keep the torque out of the can's body. Be ready for the moment the joint breaks: the wrenches swing and can pinch your hand.
deepSteps.quote: Use the Hook Spanners to catch the notches in the parts such that the adapter is being turned Counter-Clockwise and the suppressor Clock- wise.
deepSteps.cite: NOMAD Ti XC  SERIES  OWNERS MANUAL — Rev071824 — 4. ADAPTER REMOVAL, printed p.7
deepSteps.warn: WHEN THE TORQUE BREAKS BETWEEN THE TWO PARTS, THE WRENCHES MAY SWING ENOUGH TO CREATE A PINCH POINT. ALWAYS BE CAREFUL AND MIND THE GAP!

deepSteps.title: Stuck adapter: heat, and mind the hot surfaces
deepSteps.action: If the threads will not let go, Dead Air allows heating the suppressor to loosen them. Handle it only by the spanners once it is hot.
deepSteps.prose: Heat is the maker's answer to a seized mount, not a longer lever. More force on cold, locked threads is how the notches get torn up.
deepSteps.quote: YOU MAY NEED TO HEAT THE SUPPRESSOR UP TO LOOSEN THE THREADS. PAY SPECIAL ATTENTION TO THE HEATED SURFACES TO AVOID BURNS!
deepSteps.cite: NOMAD Ti XC  SERIES  OWNERS MANUAL — Rev071824 — 4. ADAPTER REMOVAL, printed p.7

deepSteps.title: Front cap off with the pinned tool
deepSteps.action: Fit the pins of the Sandman Front Cap Tool (DA208, sold separately) into the holes in the front cap. Hold the tool flat against the cap with the pins evenly and fully engaged, and turn counter-clockwise to loosen and remove it.
deepSteps.prose: Flat and fully engaged is the whole instruction. A tool sitting proud on one pin slips and chews the holes in the cap.
deepSteps.quote: Align the pins in the Sandman Front Cap Tool (DA208—sold separately) into the holes cut into the front cap.
deepSteps.cite: NOMAD Ti XC  SERIES  OWNERS MANUAL — Rev071824 — 5. FRONT CAP INSTALLATION, printed p.8

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Clean the threads and taper, then grease
deepSteps.action: With the cap off, clean its threads and taper, put a high-quality grease on those surfaces, and hand-tighten the cap back in. When an adapter comes out, clean its threads the same way before a mount goes back in.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ Debris on a thread or a taper throws the parts out of line, and a part out of line is what a bullet hits. Clean surfaces are the reason these parts ever come off.
deepSteps.quote: Clean threads and taper. Apply high quality grease to the surfaces and install new cap and hand tighten.
deepSteps.cite: NOMAD Ti XC  SERIES  OWNERS MANUAL — Rev071824 — 5. FRONT CAP INSTALLATION, printed p.8
deepSteps.warn: DEBRIS ON THE THREADS AND TAPER SURFACES MAY CAUSE MISALIGNMENT OF SUPPRESSOR PARTS AND ALLOW FOR PROJECTILE STRIKES ON BAFFLES OR THE FRONT CAP.

deepSteps.title: Adapter back in: grease, bottom out, opposed spanners
deepSteps.action: Coat the adapter's threads with high-quality grease and thread it into the back of the suppressor until it bottoms out on the rear face. Tighten with the hook spanners, this time turning the adapter clockwise and the suppressor counter-clockwise.
deepSteps.prose: ⚠ HUB-taper adapters bottom out on a taper inside the can instead, which leaves a gap between the notched flange and the rear face. On those versions the gap is correct and is not a loose adapter.
deepSteps.quote: Thread the adapter into the suppressor until it bottoms out on the rear suppressor face.
deepSteps.cite: NOMAD Ti XC  SERIES  OWNERS MANUAL — Rev071824 — 3. ADAPTER INSTALLATION, printed p.6

deepSteps.title: Thread locker only if the mount keeps loosening
deepSteps.action: If the mount loosens under heavy heat cycles, degrease the threads and use a high-temperature thread locker. For average conditions Dead Air names a medium-strength, high-temperature one, Vibra-Tite 123.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ Medium strength matters as much as high temperature. Many high-strength lockers need serious heat to break, and you may not get the adapter out again without it.
deepSteps.quote: Dead Air recommends using a medium strength, high temperature thread locker like Vibra-Tite 123 for average operating conditions.
deepSteps.cite: NOMAD Ti XC  SERIES  OWNERS MANUAL — Rev071824 — 3. ADAPTER INSTALLATION, printed p.6

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Inspection on assembly — snug, no gaps, no rattle
deepSteps.action: With everything back together, every component should be snug with no gaps and no rattle (the HUB-taper gap excepted). If anything will not tighten fully, check its threads for damage or debris, clean both mating parts and tighten again.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ This is the check before live fire. A rattle on the bench is a baffle strike at the range.
deepSteps.quote: All components should be snug with no gaps or rattling. If any component is not fully tightened, then check threads for any damage or debris.
deepSteps.cite: NOMAD Ti XC  SERIES  OWNERS MANUAL — Rev071824 — 6. INSPECTION UPON ASSEMBLY, printed p.8

cleaning.name: MOUNT & THREADS
tasks: Clean the adapter threads and taper, then coat with a high-quality grease
Check tightness often — direct-thread mounts loosen with use
⛔ Debris on a thread or taper misaligns the parts and invites a baffle strike

cleaning.name: FRONT CAP
tasks: Remove only with the pinned front cap tool (DA208), held flat with the pins fully engaged
Clean threads and taper, grease, hand-tighten
Store the cap not in service on the tool itself

cleaning.name: BODY
tasks: Do not open the baffle core — Dead Air publishes no procedure for it
Wipe the exterior; check for looseness, gaps or rattle before every use
Anything that will not tighten or sit straight goes to Dead Air's Customer Service Department

reassembly: Grease the adapter threads, thread the adapter into the back of the can until it bottoms out, and tighten it with the hook spanners — adapter clockwise, suppressor counter-clockwise.
Clean and grease the front cap's threads and taper, then hand-tighten the cap.
Inspect: every component snug, no gaps, no rattle (the HUB-taper gap excepted).
Clean and lube the rifle's muzzle threads, thread the can on by hand without cross threading until it is tight against the shoulder, and never past 30 ft-lbs — 25 +/- 5 ft-lbs is the target.
Look at the mounted can: it must sit straight on the centreline of the bore, not canted.
fncheck: Rifle unloaded and the can cold: grip the suppressor and try to turn, shake and wobble it. It must be firmly and rigidly mounted with no rattle, and it must sit straight on the centreline of the bore. If it is canted or will not thread on smoothly, stop and contact Dead Air's Customer Service Department.
